_note: Shared fill-in lines for every 11 report (all 12 Soul Urges). Keys: EX and LP = her Expression / Life Path (1-9, 11, 22; a 33 uses 6). REASON = one-digit Life Path mod 3 (11->2, 22->4, 33->6). Every line must read right in all 12 reports, so none may name or lean on one Soul Urge's subject. Frames each field drops into are in product/0-REPORT-WORKFLOW-11.md, 'The shared list'.

1.saw: a woman who went first while everyone else looked at their shoes
1.use: the part of you that stepped up so they didn't have to
1.letter: you never waited to be told. You'd already started before anybody else had made up their mind.

2.saw: a woman who'd sit still and really listen, and make room for them
2.use: your ear, the one that always had time for them
2.letter: you'd stop what you were doing when I talked. You heard the whole thing, even the parts that went nowhere.

3.saw: a woman who lit up a room and made them feel like somebody
3.use: the part of you that made them look good
3.letter: people perked up when you were around. You asked me things like my answer mattered.

4.saw: a woman who stayed put and kept her word
4.use: the part of you that showed up every single time
4.letter: you said you'd be there and you were. You weren't going anywhere, and I knew it.

5.saw: a woman with some life in her, game for just about anything
5.use: the part of you that livened things up for them
5.letter: you were up for anything. Whatever I came up with, you were in before I'd finished saying it.

6.saw: a woman who took care of everybody and never kept score
6.use: all the ways you made their life easier
6.letter: you saw to everybody. Whoever needed something got it, and you never made anybody feel they owed you.

7.saw: a woman who noticed things other people walked right past
7.use: the part of you that noticed what they missed
7.letter: you caught the little things nobody else did. Not much got by you.

8.saw: a woman who could walk into a mess and straighten it out
8.use: the part of you that got things done
8.letter: you were the one who handled things. Something needed doing, you did it, no fuss.

9.saw: a woman who'd give to anybody and look for the good in them first
9.use: the part of you that kept on giving
9.letter: you thought the best of me. Even when I hadn't earned it, you'd find some reason to.

11.saw: a woman who knew what they needed before they'd said a word
11.use: the part of you that kept track of their moods
11.letter: you could tell what was going on with me from my face. I never had to explain myself.

22.saw: a woman who could start with next to nothing and build something real
22.use: the part of you that did the heavy lifting
22.letter: you could make something out of whatever you had. You didn't wait around for it to be handed to you.

1.then: When it went wrong with them, you put your head down and handled it by yourself. You didn't call anybody or let on. If something needed fixing, you fixed it, and if you couldn't, you went without. Asking would have meant explaining, and you'd had enough of being at somebody's mercy. Doing it alone got you through, and back then it made sense.
1.now: you tell them you've got it before they've even offered, and soon enough they take you at your word and leave you be
1.letter: When something went wrong, you dealt with it and I heard about it after, if I heard at all. You never once came to me with it. I'd made sure coming to me got you nowhere.

2.then: When it went wrong with them, you said yes before you'd had a chance to think, and then lay awake sore about it. You kept checking where you stood, reading every look for a sign you were still liked. Keeping the peace kept things from getting worse, and when you didn't know what else to do, it was how you held on.
2.now: you go along with all of it, then hold it against them on the quiet, till they feel something's off and drift away without ever knowing what
2.letter: You'd agree to anything I said, and a day later it'd come out sideways. You kept asking if we were okay. I never gave you a straight answer, and I knew what that did to you.

3.then: When it went wrong with them, you made a joke of it before anybody else could. You filled every day so full there wasn't a quiet minute left to think in. People asked and got the funny version, and the real thing stayed put. That got you through. If you'd stopped long enough to say it, you'd have had to feel it, and you weren't ready to.
3.now: you crack a joke the minute it gets close to anything real, and after a while they quit trying
3.letter: When something bothered you, you'd get funny and find a job that needed doing. I don't think I ever heard you say what was really wrong. I never asked. It was easier on me that way.

4.then: When it went wrong with them, you got organized. You made rules for yourself and stuck to them. You worked till you dropped and went back over everything a second time, then checked it again. If every last thing was done right, nothing could catch you out. When nothing else would hold still, that was something you could hold on to, and it worked.
4.now: you've got a way things have to be done, and you watch how they do it, till they feel checked up on and give up
4.letter: When something got to you, you'd start making lists. You'd do things over that were fine the first time, and you wouldn't let up till it was all just so. A lot of what you were holding together was my mess. I know that.

5.then: When it went wrong with them, you changed the scenery. Different place, different people, and every time you meant it to be the clean start. Sitting still meant sitting in it, and you couldn't. Moving on gave you air when you were short of it, and it got you out from under something heavy. Back then, that was the right instinct.
5.now: you're itching to go the minute things start to feel ordinary, and they're left standing there wondering what they did
5.letter: When something got to you, you were halfway out the door before anybody knew anything was wrong. A lot of the time it was me you were getting away from. I can see that now.

6.then: When it went wrong with them, you took care of everybody in sight. If people were busy being helped by you, nobody was close enough to see how you were doing. You ran yourself ragged, and some nights you were fed up with all of them and never said so. Being the one everybody needed gave you somewhere to stand, and it kept you going.
6.now: you jump in and start taking care of them, and there's never an opening for them to do a thing for you, so they go find somebody who'll let them
6.letter: When something upset you, you'd go make yourself useful to somebody. Everybody got your time but you, and you'd end up worn out and mad about it. I let you carry me right along with the rest of them. That's on me.

7.then: When it went wrong with them, you clammed up, chewed on it, and wouldn't move till you were sure. You had good reason to. Late at night, on your own, you went over it and over it, hunting for the one thing that would settle it. You'd been hurt, and going quiet kept you standing while it had to.
7.now: you clam up and wait till you're sure of them, and before long you've found what's wrong with them
7.letter: When something got to you, you'd go real quiet. You'd turn it over in your head for days and you wouldn't budge, not till you knew for certain. I gave you plenty to turn over. I know that too.

8.then: When it went wrong with them, you took the wheel and kept both hands on it. You made the decisions, you kept everything running, and you didn't let one person see you need a thing. If you were in charge, nobody could pull the floor out from under you again. Staying on top of it held you together when you had every reason to fold.
8.now: you take over everything and won't let them so much as carry a bag for you, till they feel like hired help and stop coming around
8.letter: When something knocked you down, you'd grab the reins tighter. I never once saw you ask anybody for a hand. With me around, you'd have been a fool to. I'm the one who taught you that.

9.then: When it went wrong with them, you gave. You gave to good causes and to people you'd never meet, to anybody whose story got to you, and you meant every bit of it. Up close was another matter. You kept the people nearby at a little distance, even the good ones. Giving from a distance let you go on caring at all, after caring up close had cost you so much.
9.now: you're kind to them the way you're kind to strangers, warm but at arm's length, and the first time they let you down, you're done
9.letter: When something got to you, you'd go do something good for a stranger. You never expected much from the people right in front of you. I'm a big part of the reason.

11.then: When it went wrong with them, you started reading into everything. A short answer or a door shut a little too hard, and you'd be up half the night working out what it meant. Most of the time there was something there to see. Watching that close was how you saw trouble coming before it got to you, and back then you needed that.
11.now: you read a whole lot into one offhand thing they say, and they get tired of answering for things they never meant
11.letter: Anything bothered you and you'd go hunting for what it meant. A look from me could put you off for a week, and I knew it. I gave you reasons to keep watching me. I won't pretend I didn't.

22.then: When it went wrong with them, you worked the whole thing out in your head, a long way down the road, and wouldn't start anything till every piece was in place. Other people saw you standing still. To you it was the only way not to get caught out twice, and it made sense.
22.now: you need to know how it all ends before you'll take one step with them, and they get tired of waiting at the starting line
22.letter: When something shook you, you'd sit down and think it through from start to finish before you'd so much as move. With me you never knew where anything was headed. That part's mine.

0.headline: they're too proud to be the one in the wrong
0.letter: I'm too proud. I've never once gone to anybody hat in hand, and I'm not going to start with you.

1.headline: they can't stand to be looked at by the one person who knows
1.letter: I can't face you. You know what I did, and you'd look at me like you know it.

2.headline: doing nothing doesn't cost them a thing
2.letter: Nothing happens to me if I leave it be, and I've always taken the easy way out.
